title: Apparently he's busy
goal: At the office, Maryam asks whether the client has replied to your proposal; answer without promising more than you know
tip: Hedge with a chunk before the clause: iẓ-ẓāhir innah mashghūl 'apparently he's busy'; ḥasab ʿilmi, lil-ḥīn ma radd 'as far as I know, he hasn't replied yet'. When you can't promise: ma aẓman, bas fī iḥtimāl kbīr 'I can't promise, but there's a good chance'.
grammar: hedging: iẓ-ẓāhir inn, ḥasab ʿilmi, mub mitʼakkid, fī iḥtimāl
dialogue: A
صباح الخير. العميل رد على العرض اللي طرشناه؟
ṣabāḥ il-khēr. il-ʿamīl radd ʿala l-ʿarẓ illi ṭarrashnāh?
Morning. Has the client replied about the proposal we sent?
B
صباح النور. حسب علمي، للحين ما رد
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. ḥasab ʿilmi, lil-ḥīn ma radd
Morning. As far as I know, he hasn't replied yet.
A
غريبة! قال لنا بيرد قبل الويكند، والإدارة كل يوم تسألني عنه
gharība! gāl-lana biyrudd gabil il-wīkind, w il-idāra kill yōm tisʼalni ʿannah
Odd! He told us he'd reply before the weekend, and the management asks me about it every day.
B
الظاهر إنه مشغول هالأيام
iẓ-ẓāhir innah mashghūl hal-ayyām
Apparently he's busy these days.
A
يمكن. بس بيوقعون العقد ولّا لا؟ شو رأيك؟
yimkin. bas biywaggʿūn il-ʿagid walla la? shu raʼyak?
Maybe. But will they sign the contract or not? What do you think?
B
ما أضمن، بس في احتمال كبير. طلبوا نسخة ثانية حق مديرهم
ma aẓman, bas fī iḥtimāl kbīr. ṭalabaw nuskha thānya ḥagg mudīrhum
I can't promise, but there's a good chance. They asked for another copy for their manager.
A
مبدئيا هذا شي زين. يعني عجبهم العرض؟
mabdaʼiyyan hādha shay zēn. yaʿni ʿijabhum il-ʿarẓ?
In principle that's a good thing. So they liked the proposal?
B
مب متأكد، بس الظاهر إن السعر عجبهم
mub mitʼakkid, bas iẓ-ẓāhir inn is-siʿir ʿijabhum
I'm not sure, but it looks like they liked the price.
A
زين. إذا ما ردوا لين الأحد، بتواصل وياهم بنفسي
zēn. idha ma raddaw lēn il-aḥad, batwāṣal wiyyāhum b-nafsi
OK. If they haven't replied by Sunday, I'll get in touch with them myself.
B
فكرة زينة. وإن شاء الله يكون خبر حلو
fikra zēna. w in shāʼ allāh ykūn khabar ḥilu
Good idea. And hopefully it'll be good news.
items: apparently, it looks like (+ a clause)
with a pronoun: iẓ-ẓāhir innah (he, it), iẓ-ẓāhir innhum (they)
I'm not sure (said by a man)
a woman says: mub mitʼakkda (مب متأكدة)
I can't promise, I can't guarantee (it)
I can't promise you: ma aẓman-lak (ما أضمن لك) to a man
there's a good chance, it's quite likely
in principle, on the face of it
I'll get in touch with them, I'll contact them
culture: In everyday Emirati speech, in shāʼ allāh does several jobs: a plan that's already made, a polite hope, or, when it's drawn out (in shāʼ allāāh…), a gentle way of not promising. Listen to the tone, and to whether a time or a next step comes with it.

title: Something's definitely up
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, Rāshid can't stop smiling at his phone; guess with his father what has happened
tip: Guess from what you can see: wāẓiḥ innah farḥān 'he's clearly happy'; akīd fī shay 'something's definitely up'. To push a guess away: ashukk innah min il-madrasa 'I doubt it's about school'.
grammar: guessing from evidence: wāẓiḥ inn, akīd fī shay, ashukk inn
dialogue: A
شوف راشد، من الصبح يبتسم ويطالع تلفونه وما يقول شي
shūf Rāshid, min iṣ-ṣubḥ yibtisim w yṭāliʿ tilifōnah w ma ygūl shay
Look at Rāshid: since this morning he's been smiling at his phone and not saying a thing.
B
واضح إنه فرحان، يا عمي
wāẓiḥ innah farḥān, yā ʿammi
He's clearly happy, uncle.
A
أكيد في شي. بس شو؟ سره في بير هالولد
akīd fī shay. bas shu? sirrah fi bīr hal-walad
Something's definitely up. But what? This boy keeps his secrets well.
B
يمكن النتايج طلعت؟
yimkin in-natāyij ṭilʿat?
Maybe the results have come out?
A
لا، النتايج بعد أسبوعين. والمدرسة خلصت
la, in-natāyij baʿd usbūʿēn. w il-madrasa khilṣat
No, the results are in two weeks. And school's over.
B
عيل أشك إنه من المدرسة. يمكن الكورس اللي قدم عليه؟
ʿayal ashukk innah min il-madrasa. yimkin il-kōrs illi gaddam ʿalēh?
Then I doubt it's about school. Maybe the course he applied for?
A
أي كورس؟ ما قال لي عن أي كورس
ay kōrs? ma gāl-li ʿan ay kōrs
What course? He didn't tell me about any course.
B
كورس برمجة في الصيف. ساعدته في الطلب الشهر اللي طاف
kōrs barmaja fi ṣ-ṣēf. sāʿadtah fi ṭ-ṭalab ish-shahar illi ṭāf
A programming course in the summer. I helped him with the application last month.
A
راشد! تعال... يقول قبلوه! والله ما قال لأحد
Rāshid! taʿāl... ygūl gibalōh! wallāh ma gāl l-aḥad
Rāshid! Come here... He says they've accepted him! He really didn't tell anyone.
B
الله يوفقه! كنت متأكد إنه بينقبل
allāh ywaffgah! kint mitʼakkid innah biyingibil
Good for him! I was sure he'd get in.
items: about a woman: wāẓiḥ innha (واضح إنها)
something's definitely up, there must be something
I doubt (that) he…, I doubt (that) it…
he keeps his secrets well (lit. his secret is in a well)
your secret's safe with me: sirrak fi bīr (سرك في بير); (recognise)
he applied for it (a course, a job)
they've accepted him, he got in
he'll get in, he'll be accepted

title: Nothing official yet
goal: At the office, Maryam has heard the company may keep on two interns next year; find out where the news came from and how sure it is
tip: Say where news comes from: mithil ma simaʿt 'from what I heard', ʿala gōlat-ha 'as she puts it', and how solid it is: ma fī shay rasmi 'nothing's official'. Then don't get carried away: la tifraḥ wāyid, lēn yṣīr rasmi.
grammar: reporting what you've heard: mithil ma simaʿt, ʿala gōlat-ha, ma fī shay rasmi
dialogue: A
عندي لك خبر. يقولون إن الشركة بتثبت ثنين من المتدربين السنة الياية
ʿindi lak khabar. ygūlūn inn ish-sharika bitthabbit thnēn min il-mutadarrbīn is-sana l-yāya
I've got news for you. They say the company will keep on two of the interns next year.
B
لا والله! منو قال لج؟
la wallāh! minu gāl-lich?
No way! Who told you?
A
سارة من شؤون الموظفين. على قولتها، القرار في يناير
Sāra min shuʼūn il-muwaẓẓafīn. ʿala gōlat-ha, il-garār fi yanāyir
Sāra from HR. As she puts it, the decision's in January.
B
يعني الخبر أكيد؟
yaʿni l-khabar akīd?
So the news is certain?
A
لا، للحين ما في شي رسمي. أنا سامعة إن الإدارة راضية عن المتدربين هالسنة
la, lil-ḥīn ma fī shay rasmi. ana sāmʿa inn il-idāra rāẓya ʿan il-mutadarrbīn has-sana
No, nothing's official yet. I've heard the management is happy with this year's interns.
B
حلو! بس مثل ما سمعتي، منو بيختارون؟
ḥilu! bas mithil ma simaʿti, minu biykhtārūn?
Great! But from what you heard, who will they choose?
A
الظاهر اللي شغلهم زين ويداومون على الوقت
iẓ-ẓāhir illi shughulhum zēn w ydāwmūn ʿala l-wagt
Apparently the ones whose work is good and who come in on time.
B
زين. بس ما بفرح لين يصير رسمي
zēn. bas ma bafraḥ lēn yṣīr rasmi
OK. But I won't celebrate until it's official.
A
صح، لا تفرح وايد. الكلام يطير بسرعة هني
ṣaḥḥ, la tifraḥ wāyid. il-kalām yṭīr b-surʿa hni
Right, don't get your hopes up. Talk spreads fast here.
B
هيه، ومثل ما سمعت، محد يدري بشي!
hē, w mithil ma simaʿt, maḥḥad yadri b-shay!
Yes, and as far as I've heard, nobody knows a thing!
items: from what I heard, as I heard it; from what you heard (to a man)
to a woman: mithil ma simaʿti (مثل ما سمعتي)
as she puts it, according to her
about a man: ʿala gōltah (على قولته)
don't get your hopes up, don't celebrate too soon (to a man)
to a woman: la tifraḥīn wāyid (لا تفرحين وايد)
I've heard (that), word is (that) (said by a woman)
a man says: sāmiʿ inn (سامع إن); (recognise)
talk spreads fast, news travels fast (lit. talk flies fast)

title: Fahad's bet
goal: On a video call, Fahad asks if Sēf knows about the farewell dinner Bū Rāshid is planning for him; weigh up his Kuwaiti guesses
tip: Fahad guesses the Kuwaiti way, with chūd: chūd yadri 'I bet he knows'. You hedge your own way: ma astabʿid innah ḥāss b-shay 'I wouldn't be surprised if he's picked up on something', or deny it: ma ʿindah khabar 'he has no idea'.
grammar: epistemic chūd (Kuwait, recognise); ma astabʿid, ma ʿindah khabar
dialogue: A
هلا والله! شلونك؟
hala wallāh! shlōnak?
Hi there! How are you?
B
هلا بك! زين الحمد لله، وانت؟
hala bik! zēn il-ḥamdu lillāh, w inta?
Hi! Fine, thank God, and you?
A
تمام. اسمع، سيف يدري عن العشا اللي بيسويه بو راشد يوم الخميس؟
tamām. ismaʿ, Sēf yadri ʿan il-ʿasha illi biysawwīh Bū Rāshid yōm il-khamīs?
Great. Listen, does Sēf know about the dinner Bū Rāshid's giving on Thursday?
B
لا، ما عنده خبر. محد قال له
la, ma ʿindah khabar. maḥḥad gāl-lah
No, he has no idea. Nobody's told him.
A
جود يدري ويسوي عمره ما يدري! سيف ذكي، ترا
chūd yadri w ysawwi ʿumrah ma yadri! Sēf dhaki, tara
I bet he knows and he's pretending not to! Sēf's clever, you know.
B
صح ذكي، بس في هالأشيا على نياته
ṣaḥḥ dhaki, bas fi hal-ashya ʿala nyātah
True, he's clever, but with this sort of thing he's naive.
A
جود أمه قالت له. الأمهات ما يقدرون يسكتون
chūd ummah gālat-lah. il-ummahāt ma yigdarūn ysiktūn
I bet his mother told him. Mums can't keep quiet.
B
لا، أم سيف تبيها مفاجأة. واضح إنها متحمسة
la, Umm Sēf tabīha mufājaʼa. wāẓiḥ innha mitḥammsa
No, Umm Sēf wants it to be a surprise. She's clearly excited.
A
زين، عيل ما راح أقول له شي. بس جود أتأخر شوي، عندي دوام
zēn, ʿayal ma rāḥ agūl-lah shay. bas chūd atʼakhkhar shwayy, ʿindi dawām
OK, then I won't say a thing to him. But I might be a bit late; I've got work.
B
ما أستبعد إنه حاس بشي، بس ما عليه. المهم إنك تيي
ma astabʿid innah ḥāss b-shay, bas ma ʿalēh. il-muhimm innak tiyi
I wouldn't be surprised if he's picked up on something, but never mind. The main thing is that you come.
items: I bet he knows, he probably knows (Kuwait)
chūd + any verb: chūd atʼakhkhar (جود أتأخر) 'I might be late'; (recognise)
he has no idea, he knows nothing about it
about a woman: ma ʿind-ha khabar (ما عندها خبر)
I wouldn't be surprised, I wouldn't rule it out
with a clause: ma astabʿid innah… (ما أستبعد إنه)
he's picked up on something, he senses something
naive, trusting, he takes things at face value
about a woman: ʿala nyāt-ha (على نياتها)
I won't say a thing to him (Kuwait)
UAE: ma bagūl-lah shay (ما بقول له شي); (recognise)
culture: Kuwaiti and other Gulf speakers have a guessing word, chūd (جود), that the Emirati cast doesn't use: chūd yadri 'I bet he knows', chūd atʼakhkhar 'I might be late'. Learn to hear it from Fahad and Nūra; for your own guesses, keep to yimkin, iẓ-ẓāhir and ma astabʿid.

title: Too good to be true
goal: At a karak stand, Sēf shows you an ad promising easy money from home; say why you doubt it, without making fun of him
tip: Doubt politely, then give a reason: ashukk fīh 'I doubt it'; kalām fāẓi 'that's nonsense' is for friends. Reason with lō: lō kān ṣij, chān killna sawwēnāh 'if it were true, we'd all have done it'.
grammar: doubt and disbelief: ashukk fīh, mub manṭigi, kalām fāẓi
dialogue: A
شوف هالإعلان! يقولون تربح خمسة آلاف في الأسبوع من البيت
shūf hal-iʿlān! ygūlūn tirbaḥ khamsat ālāf fi l-usbūʿ min il-bēt
Look at this ad! They say you earn five thousand a week from home.
B
خمسة آلاف؟ أشك فيه
khamsat ālāf? ashukk fīh
Five thousand? I doubt it.
A
ليش؟ حاطين صور ناس ربحوا، والأرباح مضمونة على كلامهم
lēsh? ḥāṭṭīn ṣuwar nās ribḥaw, w il-arbāḥ maẓmūna ʿala kalāmhum
Why? They've put up photos of people who made money, and the profits are guaranteed, so they say.
B
يا ريّال، هذا كلام فاضي
yā rayyāl, hādha kalām fāẓi
Come on, man, that's nonsense.
A
بس يبون مية درهم بس عشان تبدا
bas yabūn miyat dirham bas ʿashān tibda
But they only want a hundred dirhams for you to start.
B
هني المشكلة. مب منطقي، ما في شي ببلاش
hni l-mushkila. mub manṭigi, ma fī shay b-balāsh
That's the problem. It doesn't make sense; nothing's for free.
A
يمكن صج، ما تدري
yimkin ṣij, ma tadri
Maybe it's true, you never know.
B
لو كان صج، جان كلنا سويناه
lō kān ṣij, chān killna sawwēnāh
If it were true, we'd all have done it.
A
هههه، معك حق. الظاهر إنه نصب
hhhh, maʿak ḥagg. iẓ-ẓāhir innah naṣb
Haha, you're right. It looks like a scam.
B
هيه، لا تحط فيه ولا درهم
hē, la tḥuṭṭ fīh wala dirham
Yes, don't put a single dirham into it.
items: I doubt it, I'm not sure about it (m.)
about a feminine thing: ashukk fīha (أشك فيها)
it doesn't make sense, it's not logical
you earn, you make money; you win (to a man)
so they say, according to them
don't put a single dirham into it (to a man)
to a woman: la tḥuṭṭīn fīh wala dirham
task: This week: search YouTube for «سوالف» or «بودكاست إماراتي». Listen for 10 minutes and note every time a speaker hedges or doubts (yimkin, iẓ-ẓāhir, ashukk, ma aẓunn, ḥasab ʿilmi). Write down three sentences around them. Within a minute you should hear شو / مب (UAE) or شنو / مو (Kuwait); if you hear سوف, ليس or هل all the time, it's fuṣḥā: pick another clip.

title: He told me himself
goal: On the metro with Sēf, you disagree about which night Bū Rāshid's dinner is; back up your version by saying where you heard it
tip: Say how you know: gālha-li b-nafsah 'he told me himself', simaʿt-ha minnah b-idhni 'I heard it from him with my own ears'. Ask the other side: min wēn simaʿt? And bet on it: idha ṭilaʿt ghalṭān 'if I turn out to be wrong'.
grammar: certainty and its source: b-nafsah, b-idhni, min wēn simaʿt?
dialogue: A
عشا عمي يوم الجمعة، صح؟
ʿasha ʿammi yōm il-jumʿa, ṣaḥḥ?
My uncle's dinner is on Friday, right?
B
لا، يوم الخميس. أضمن لك
la, yōm il-khamīs. aẓman-lak
No, on Thursday. Take it from me.
A
انت غلطان. أنا سمعت الجمعة
inta ghalṭān. ana simaʿt il-jumʿa
You're wrong. I heard Friday.
B
من وين سمعت؟
min wēn simaʿt?
Where did you hear that?
A
ما أذكر بالضبط. يمكن من راشد، أو يمكن أنا خربطت
ma adhkur biẓ-ẓabṭ. yimkin min Rāshid, aw yimkin ana kharbaṭt
I don't remember exactly. Maybe from Rāshid, or maybe I got it mixed up.
B
عمك قالها لي بنفسه في المجلس
ʿammak gālha-li b-nafsah fi l-majlis
Your uncle told me himself, in the majlis.
A
زين، بس ذاكرتك مب أحسن من ذاكرتي!
zēn, bas dhākirtak mub aḥsan min dhākirti!
OK, but your memory's no better than mine!
B
إذا طلعت غلطان، أعزمك على كرك أسبوع كامل
idha ṭilaʿt ghalṭān, aʿazmak ʿala karak usbūʿ kāmil
If I turn out to be wrong, I'll buy you karak for a whole week.
A
اتفقنا! بطرش لعمي وبنشوف منو الصح
ittafagna! baṭarrish l-ʿammi w binshūf minu ṣ-ṣaḥḥ
Deal! I'll message my uncle and we'll see who's right.
B
طرش. أنا سمعتها منه بأذني
ṭarrish. ana simaʿt-ha minnah b-idhni
Go ahead. I heard it from him with my own ears.
items: he told me himself, he told me in person
she told me herself: gālat-ha-li b-nafs-ha (قالتها لي بنفسها)
where did you hear that? (to a man)
to a woman: min wēn simaʿti? (من وين سمعتي؟)
to a woman: inti ghalṭāna (انتي غلطانة)
if I turn out to be wrong (said by a man)
a woman says: idha ṭilaʿt ghalṭāna (إذا طلعت غلطانة)
I heard it from him with my own ears
I got (it) mixed up, I muddled it; you got it mixed up (to a man)

title: May God make it easy for him
goal: At Sēf's family home, with Sēf upstairs packing, Umm Sēf tells you she's worried about him going; answer her worry with blessings
tip: Wish someone well by asking God for it: allāh ysahhil ʿalēh 'may God make it easy for him', allāh yiktib-lah illi fīh il-khēr 'may God bring him what's best'. With ʿasa + a verb: ʿasāha tkūn sana khēr 'may it be a good year'.
grammar: optatives: allāh y- + wish; ʿasa + wish
dialogue: A
هلا يا وليدي، حياك الله. سيف فوق يرتب شنطته
hala yā wlēdi, ḥayyāk allāh. Sēf fōg yrattib shanṭtah
Hello, my son, welcome. Sēf's upstairs packing his suitcase.
B
الله يحييج يا خالتي. شحالج؟
allāh yḥayyīch yā khālti. shḥālich?
Thank you, auntie. How are you?
A
بخير الحمد لله. بس قلبي مب مرتاح، الولد بيسافر بعيد
b-khēr il-ḥamdu lillāh. bas galbi mub mirtāḥ, il-walad biysāfir baʿīd
Fine, thank God. But my heart's uneasy; the boy's going far away.
B
الله يسهل عليه، ويرده لكم بالسلامة
allāh ysahhil ʿalēh, w yruddah lakum bis-salāma
May God make it easy for him, and bring him back to you safe and sound.
A
آمين. الله يوفقه ويرفع راسنا
āmīn. allāh ywaffgah w yirfaʿ rāsna
Amen. May God grant him success and make us proud.
B
إن شاء الله. هو مستعد، ويستاهل كل خير
in shāʼ allāh. huwa mistaʿidd, w yistāhil kill khēr
God willing. He's ready, and he deserves the very best.
A
الله يحفظك. وعساها تكون سنة خير عليه
allāh yiḥfaẓak. w ʿasāha tkūn sana khēr ʿalēh
God keep you. And may it be a good year for him.
B
الله يكتب له اللي فيه الخير، يا خالتي
allāh yiktib-lah illi fīh il-khēr, yā khālti
May God bring him what's best, auntie.
A
آمين يا رب... هذا هو نزل! عسى عمرك طويل، كنا نتكلم عنك
āmīn yā rabb... hādha huwa nizal! ʿasa ʿumrak ṭawīl, kinna nitkallam ʿannak
Amen... Here he is, he's come down! Speak of the devil, we were just talking about you.
B
هلا سيف! يلا، بساعدك في الشنطة
hala Sēf! yalla, basāʿdak fi sh-shanṭa
Hi Sēf! Come on, I'll help you with the suitcase.
items: may God make it easy for him
for you: allāh ysahhil ʿalēk (to a man), ʿalēch (to a woman)
(may God) bring him back to you safe and sound
about a woman: yrudd-ha lakum bis-salāma (يردها لكم بالسلامة)
الله يكتب له اللي فيه الخير
may God bring him what's best (lit. write for him what has good in it)
for you: allāh yiktib-lak illi fīh il-khēr (to a man)
may it (f.) be, I hope it'll be (+ a wish)
a masculine noun: ʿasāh ykūn (عساه يكون)
about a woman: tistāhil kill khēr (تستاهل كل خير)
my son, my boy (an older person to a young man)
speak of the devil! (kindly; lit. may your life be long)
said to someone who turns up as you mention him; (recognise)
culture: Before a journey, many Muslims say the travel prayer (duʿāʼ as-safar), asking God for protection on the way. When someone is about to leave, family and friends add their own blessings, as Umm Sēf and you do here: may God make it easy for him and bring him back safe.

title: God be pleased with you
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, he thanks you for helping Rāshid with his course; take his thanks and bless him back
tip: An elder thanks you with a blessing: allāh yirẓa ʿalēk, allāh yisʿidak. Play it down (hādha aqall shay) and bless him back: āmīn w iyyāk, allāh yṭawwil ʿumrak. When he says mā gaṣṣart, the reply is still mā sawwēna shay.
grammar: optatives as thanks: allāh yisʿidak, allāh yṭawwil ʿumrak, allāh yhannīh
dialogue: A
حياك الله يا ولدي! راشد ما وقف يسولف عنك
ḥayyāk allāh yā wildi! Rāshid ma wigaf ysōlif ʿannak
Welcome, son! Rāshid hasn't stopped talking about you.
B
الله يحييك يا عمي. شحالك؟
allāh yḥayyīk yā ʿammi. shḥālak?
Thank you, uncle. How are you?
A
بخير الله يسلمك. الله يرضى عليك، ساعدته في طلب الكورس
b-khēr allāh ysallmak. allāh yirẓa ʿalēk, sāʿadtah fi ṭalab il-kōrs
Fine, thank you. God bless you, you helped him with the course application.
B
هذا أقل شي يا عمي. راشد يستاهل
hādha aqall shay yā ʿammi. Rāshid yistāhil
It's the least I could do, uncle. Rāshid deserves it.
A
لا والله، تعبت وياه وايد. الله يسعدك مثل ما فرحتنا
la wallāh, tiʿabt wiyyāh wāyid. allāh yisʿidak mithil ma farraḥtna
No, really, you went to a lot of trouble for him. May God make you happy, as you've made us happy.
B
آمين وإياك يا عمي. الله يطول عمرك
āmīn w iyyāk yā ʿammi. allāh yṭawwil ʿumrak
Amen, and you too, uncle. God give you a long life.
A
ويقول إنك عطيته اللابتوب حقك؟
w ygūl innak ʿaṭētah il-lābtōb ḥaggak?
And he says you gave him your laptop?
B
هيه، عندي واحد يديد، وهو يحتاجه للكورس
hē, ʿindi wāḥid yidīd, w huwa yiḥtājah lil-kōrs
Yes, I've got a new one, and he needs it for the course.
A
الله يخلف عليك. ما قصرت والله
allāh yikhlif ʿalēk. mā gaṣṣart wallāh
May God repay you. You've been so kind, truly.
B
ما سوينا شي يا عمي. الله يهنيه فيه
mā sawwēna shay yā ʿammi. allāh yhannīh fīh
It was nothing, uncle. I hope he enjoys it.
items: God bless you (warm thanks, usually from an older person) (to a man)
to a woman: allāh yirẓa ʿalēch (الله يرضى عليج); (recognise)
it's the least I could do
you went to a lot of trouble for him (to a man)
to a woman: tiʿabti wiyyāh (تعبتي وياه)
God make you happy (warm thanks) (to a man)
to a woman: allāh yisʿidich (الله يسعدج)
as you've made us happy (to a man)
to a woman: mithil ma farraḥtīna (مثل ما فرحتينا); (recognise)
God give you a long life (thanks, to an older man)
to a woman: allāh yṭawwil ʿumrich (الله يطول عمرج)
may God repay you (for what you've given or spent) (to a man)
to a woman: allāh yikhlif ʿalēch; (recognise)
may he enjoy it (said of something given to him)
to the person himself: allāh yhannīk (الله يهنيك)

title: Come on, keep going!
goal: On a video call, Rāshid says his programming course is too hard after one week and he wants to quit; talk him into carrying on
tip: Urge a friend on with commands: shidd ḥēlak! 'come on, keep at it!', inta gaddha 'you can do it'. Stop him with la + verb: la twaggif il-ḥīn 'don't stop now', la tgārin nafsak fīhum 'don't compare yourself with them'.
grammar: urging: shidd ḥēlak, inta gaddha, la + verb
dialogue: A
برو، الكورس صعب وايد. أفكر أطلع منه
brō, il-kōrs ṣaʿb wāyid. afakkir aṭlaʿ minnah
Bro, the course is really hard. I'm thinking of dropping out.
B
تطلع؟ بعد أسبوع واحد بس؟
tiṭlaʿ? baʿd usbūʿ wāḥid bas?
Drop out? After just one week?
A
مليت! كل يوم كود، ودماغي بينفجر
malēt! kill yōm kōd, w dmāghi biyinfijir
I'm fed up! Code every day, and my brain's going to explode.
B
عادي، أول أسبوع دايما صعب
ʿādi, awwal usbūʿ dāyman ṣaʿb
That's normal; the first week's always hard.
A
بس الشباب الثانيين أشطر مني
bas ish-shabāb ith-thānyīn ashṭar minni
But the other guys are better than me.
B
لا تقارن نفسك فيهم. شد حيلك!
la tgārin nafsak fīhum. shidd ḥēlak!
Don't compare yourself with them. Come on, keep at it!
A
وإذا ما فهمت شي؟
w idha ma fhimt shay?
And if I don't understand something?
B
اسأل، وخذها خطوة خطوة. انت قدها
isʼal, w khidhha khaṭwa khaṭwa. inta gaddha
Ask, and take it step by step. You can do it.
A
يعني ما أطلع؟
yaʿni ma aṭlaʿ?
So I shouldn't drop out?
B
لا توقف الحين. كمل الشهر، ولا تفشلني!
la twaggif il-ḥīn. kammil ish-shahar, w la tfashshilni!
Don't stop now. Finish the month, and don't let me down!
items: come on, keep at it, put your back into it (to a man)
to a woman: shiddi ḥēlich (شدي حيلج); to a group: shiddu ḥēlkum (شدوا حيلكم)
you can do it, you're up to it (to a man)
to a woman: inti gaddha (انتي قدها)
to a woman: la tgārnīn nafsich (لا تقارنين نفسج)
to a woman: la twaggfīn (لا توقفين)
don't let me down, don't show me up (to a man) (friends only)
to a woman: la tfashshlīni (لا تفشليني)
(to) drop out of it, (to) quit it (a course)
I'm fed up, I'm sick of it
my brain's going to explode (friends only)

title: Let's begin, with God's blessing
goal: At the office, Maryam starts a new project with the team; get everyone going, share out the work and answer her good wishes
tip: Start a job together: tawakkalna ʿala llāh or ʿala barakat illāh 'off we go'. Urge with let's: khallna ngassim ish-shughul, yalla nibda; urge a group with the -u ending: shiddu ḥēlkum, la titʼakhkharūn.
grammar: hortatives: tawakkalna, ʿala barakat illāh, khallna, yalla + verb
dialogue: A
يلا يا جماعة، توكلنا على الله. المشروع اليديد يبدا اليوم
yalla yā jamāʿa, tawakkalna ʿala llāh. il-mashrūʿ il-yidīd yibda l-yōm
Right, everyone, let's get going. The new project starts today.
B
على بركة الله. شو أول شي؟
ʿala barakat illāh. shu awwal shay?
Off we go. What comes first?
A
الخطة لازم تخلص قبل الخميس، وما في وقت وايد
il-khiṭṭa lāzim tikhlaṣ gabil il-khamīs, w ma fī wagt wāyid
The plan has to be finished before Thursday, and there isn't much time.
B
عيل خلنا نقسم الشغل بيننا. كل واحد ياخذ جزء
ʿayal khallna ngassim ish-shughul bēnna. kill wāḥid yākhidh juzʼ
Then let's split the work between us. Everyone takes a part.
A
فكرة زينة. انت خذ التقرير، وأنا آخذ العرض
fikra zēna. inta khidh it-taqrīr, w ana ākhidh il-ʿarẓ
Good idea. You take the report, and I'll take the presentation.
B
تمام. وانتو يا شباب، شدوا حيلكم!
tamām. w intu yā shabāb, shiddu ḥēlkum!
Fine. And you guys, put your backs into it!
A
وأبيكم تشتغلون بحماس، ولا تتأخرون على الاجتماعات
w abīkum tishtaghlūn b-ḥamās, w la titʼakhkharūn ʿala l-ijtimāʿāt
And I want you all to work with energy, and don't be late for the meetings.
B
لا تحاتين، يوم الخميس بنكون مخلصين
la tḥātīn, yōm il-khamīs binkūn mkhallṣīn
Don't worry, by Thursday we'll be done.
A
بالتوفيق للكل. الله يعطيكم العافية
bit-tawfīg lil-kill. allāh yaʿṭīkum il-ʿāfya
Good luck, everyone. Thanks for all your hard work.
B
الله يعافيج. يلا نبدا!
allāh yʿāfīch. yalla nibda!
Thank you. Let's get started!
items: let's get going, trusting in God (as you start something)
off we go, with God's blessing (as you start something)
we'll be done, we'll have finished
a man on his own: bakūn mkhallaṣ (بكون مخلص)
there's no time, there isn't time
not much time: ma fī wagt wāyid
good luck (with it), all the best
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner (search a tutoring site for «Emirati Arabic tutor»), plan an imaginary group trip together for 10 minutes: who books what and by when. Start with tawakkalna ʿala llāh, split the jobs (kill wāḥid yākhidh…), urge them on once (shidd ḥēlak) and end with a wish (allāh ysahhil ʿalēk).

title: I swear I saw him!
goal: At a karak stand, you tell Sēf you've just seen Fahad at Dubai Mall; he won't believe you, so insist
tip: Insist with an oath and a fact: wallāh il-ʿaẓīm shiftah 'I swear I saw him'; huwa b-nafsah 'the man himself'. Sēf doubts: min jiddak? 'are you serious?' A plain wallāh is everyday; wallāh il-ʿaẓīm is for when you really need to be believed.
grammar: insisting: wallāh il-ʿaẓīm, huwa b-nafsah, min jiddak?
dialogue: B
سيف، شفت فهد اليوم في دبي مول!
Sēf, shift Fahad il-yōm fi Dbayy Mōl!
Sēf, I saw Fahad today at Dubai Mall!
A
فهد؟ مستحيل، فهد في الكويت. يتهيأ لك
Fahad? mustaḥīl, Fahad fi l-Kwēt. yithayyaʼ-lak
Fahad? Impossible, Fahad's in Kuwait. You're imagining things.
B
والله العظيم شفته، عند النافورة
wallāh il-ʿaẓīm shiftah, ʿind in-nāfūra
I swear to God I saw him, by the fountain.
A
يمكن واحد يشبهه. وايد ناس يلبسون نفس الشي
yimkin wāḥid yishbahah. wāyid nās yilbisūn nafs ish-shay
Maybe someone who looks like him. Lots of people wear the same thing.
B
لا، هو بنفسه. حتى سلم علي من بعيد
la, huwa b-nafsah. ḥatta sallam ʿalay min baʿīd
No, it was him, the man himself. He even waved to me from a distance.
A
من جدك؟ وليش ما قال لي إنه ياي؟
min jiddak? w lēsh ma gāl-li innah yāy?
Are you serious? Then why didn't he tell me he was coming?
B
ما أدري. بس والله العظيم إنه هو
ma adri. bas wallāh il-ʿaẓīm innah huwa
I don't know. But I swear it was him.
A
انت تحب تمزح وايد، ترا
inta tḥibb timzaḥ wāyid, tara
You do like a joke, you know.
B
هالمرة ما أمزح. صدقني!
hal-marra ma amzaḥ. ṣaddigni!
This time I'm not joking. Believe me!
A
دقيقة... فهد طرش لي: لا تقول لسيف إني في دبي! غلط في الرقم
digīga... Fahad ṭarrash-li: la tgūl l-Sēf inni fi Dbayy! ghilaṭ fi r-ragam
Hang on... Fahad's messaged me: 'Don't tell Sēf I'm in Dubai!' He sent it to the wrong number.
items: I swear to God, I swear it's true (strong)
him in person, the man himself
about a woman: hiya b-nafs-ha (هي بنفسها)
to a woman: min jiddich? (من جدج؟)
he waved to me from a distance (lit. he greeted me from afar)
he got the wrong number, he sent it to the wrong person
culture: Wallāh 'by God' is everyday Gulf talk, used for 'really' or 'honestly'; longer oaths such as wallāh il-ʿaẓīm are stronger and kept for when it matters. You may hear other oaths in films, such as ʿalayy iṭ-ṭalāg: don't use them.

title: So much that I shut up
goal: At a café, Fahad (secretly in Dubai) asks how Sēf took your news; tell him, and talk up the dinner that's coming
tip: Emphasise how far something went with lad-daraja inn: ẓiḥak ʿalay lad-daraja inni sikatt 'he laughed at me so much that I shut up'. Fahad's Kuwaiti emphasis is for recognising: kint gid ḥajazt 'I'd (really) booked', ʿazz allāh 'honestly'.
grammar: emphasis: lad-daraja inn, wala aḥla; Kuwaiti gid and ʿazz allāh (recognise)
dialogue: A
سيف ما صدقك؟
Sēf ma ṣaddagak?
Sēf didn't believe you?
B
لا، ضحك علي لدرجة إني سكت
la, ẓiḥak ʿalay lad-daraja inni sikatt
No, he laughed at me so much that I shut up.
A
زين سويت. أنا كنت قد حجزت من شهر، وما قلت لأحد
zēn sawwēt. ana kint gid ḥajazt min shahar, w ma gilt l-aḥad
Good. I'd booked a whole month ago, and I didn't tell anyone.
B
من شهر؟ وما قلت لي ولا كلمة!
min shahar? w ma gilt-li wala kilma!
A month ago? And you didn't say a word to me!
A
عز الله إني تعبت وأنا ساكت!
ʿazz allāh inni tiʿabt w ana sākit!
Honestly, keeping quiet wore me out!
B
هههه. بس العشا بيكون رهيب، ما تتخيل
hhhh. bas il-ʿasha biykūn rahīb, ma titkhayyal
Haha. But the dinner's going to be amazing, you can't imagine.
A
سمعت إن بو راشد مسوي ذبيحة كاملة؟
simaʿt inn Bū Rāshid msawwi dhbīḥa kāmla?
I heard Bū Rāshid's having a whole sheep cooked?
B
هيه، وطابخين أكل لدرجة إنه يكفي الفريج كله!
hē, w ṭābkhīn akil lad-daraja innah ykaffi l-firīj killah!
Yes, and they're cooking so much food it'll feed the whole neighbourhood!
A
عز الله إنه كريم. الله يحفظه
ʿazz allāh innah karīm. allāh yiḥfaẓah
He really is generous. God keep him.
B
الله يحفظه. بتكون ليلة ولا أحلى
allāh yiḥfaẓah. bitkūn lēla wala aḥla
God keep him. It'll be a night like no other.
items: so much that, to the point that
with a pronoun: lad-daraja inni (I), lad-daraja innah (he, it)
a month ago; for a month now
keeping quiet, without saying a word (said by a man)
a woman says: w ana sākta (وأنا ساكتة)
to a woman: ma titkhayylīn (ما تتخيلين)
like no other, couldn't be better (after a noun)
a slaughtered sheep, a whole sheep (cooked for guests)

title: Nothing special, uncle
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, he praises your Arabic and your work; accept the praise modestly and pass the credit on
tip: Take praise by playing it down: min dhōgak 'that's kind of you', bas mub dhāk iz-zōd 'but it's nothing special'. Pass the credit on: shay basīṭ, w Maryam sāʿadatni; killah minkum 'it's all thanks to you'.
grammar: understatement: mub dhāk iz-zōd, min dhōgak, killah minkum
dialogue: A
ما شاء الله تبارك الرحمن! سولفت مع الشواب ساعة كاملة
mā shāʼ allāh tabārak ir-raḥmān! sōlaft maʿa sh-shuwwāb sāʿa kāmla
Mā shāʼ allāh, God bless! You chatted with the old men for a whole hour.
B
من ذوقك يا عمي. بس مب ذاك الزود
min dhōgak yā ʿammi. bas mub dhāk iz-zōd
That's kind of you, uncle. But it's nothing special.
A
لا والله، صرت تتكلم مثلنا
la wallāh, ṣirt titkallam mithilna
No, really, you speak like us now.
B
بعدني أغلط وايد. بس أحاول
baʿadni aghlaṭ wāyid. bas aḥāwil
I still make lots of mistakes. But I try.
A
الكل يغلط. المهم إنك ما تستحي تتكلم
il-kill yighlaṭ. il-muhimm innak ma tistiḥi titkallam
Everyone makes mistakes. What matters is you're not shy about speaking.
B
كله منكم يا عمي، انتو تشجعوني
killah minkum yā ʿammi, intu tshajjʿūni
It's all thanks to you, uncle; you all encourage me.
A
وسيف يقول إنك سويت العرض في الشغل بروحك؟
w Sēf ygūl innak sawwēt il-ʿarẓ fi sh-shughul b-rūḥak?
And Sēf says you did the presentation at work by yourself?
B
شي بسيط، ومريم ساعدتني وايد فيه
shay basīṭ, w Maryam sāʿadatni wāyid fīh
It was nothing much, and Maryam helped me a lot with it.
A
تواضع منك! هذي أخلاق الرياييل
tawāẓuʿ minnak! hādhi akhlāg ir-ryāyīl
You're being modest! That's how a real man behaves.
B
الله يحفظك يا عمي. مب ذاك الزود والله
allāh yiḥfaẓak yā ʿammi. mub dhāk iz-zōd wallāh
God keep you, uncle. It's nothing special, honestly.
items: that's kind of you, how nice of you to say so (to a man)
to a woman: min dhōgich (من ذوقج)
nothing special, not all that great (UAE)
you speak like us now (to a man)
to a woman: ṣirti titkallamīn mithilna
to one man: tshajjiʿni; to one woman: tshajjʿīni
you're not shy, you don't hold back (to a man)
careful: on its own, ma tistiḥi! is a rebuke, 'have you no shame?'; (recognise)
blessed be God (said with mā shāʼ allāh when praising)
the way a real man behaves (lit. men's manners)
culture: Praise in the Gulf usually comes with mā shāʼ allāh 'God has willed it', a reminder that good things come from God and a protection against envy and the evil eye. If someone praises you or your family and forgets it, others may say it for them.

title: It's no big deal
goal: At the office, Maryam has spilt coffee on her laptop just before a client meeting; calm her down and play the problem down
tip: Shrink a problem: mub sālfa 'it's no big deal', kill shay yhūn 'it's all manageable', mub awwal marra tṣīr 'it's not the first time it's happened'. To someone who's upset: khaffifi ʿala nafsich 'go easy on yourself'.
grammar: playing down: mub sālfa, kill shay yhūn, mub awwal marra
dialogue: A
يا ويلي! كبيت القهوة على اللابتوب، والاجتماع بعد ربع ساعة!
yā wēli! kabbēt il-gahwa ʿala l-lābtōb, w il-ijtimāʿ baʿd rubʿ sāʿa!
Oh no! I've spilt coffee on the laptop, and the meeting's in a quarter of an hour!
B
لا تحاتين، مب سالفة. الملفات محفوظة؟
la tḥātīn, mub sālfa. il-malaffāt maḥfūẓa?
Don't worry, it's no big deal. Are the files saved?
A
هيه، على الإيميل. بس العرض كله كان عليه!
hē, ʿala l-īmēl. bas il-ʿarẓ killah kān ʿalēh!
Yes, in my email. But the whole presentation was on it!
B
عادي، بفتحه على لابتوبي
ʿādi, baftaḥah ʿala lābtōbi
That's fine, I'll open it on my laptop.
A
بس شكلي بيكون مب زين قدام العميل
bas shakli biykūn mub zēn jiddām il-ʿamīl
But I'm going to look bad in front of the client.
B
كل شي يهون. العميل ما بيدري بشي
kill shay yhūn. il-ʿamīl ma biydri b-shay
It's all manageable. The client won't know a thing.
A
الله يستر... وإذا خرب اللابتوب؟
allāh yistur... w idha khirab il-lābtōb?
Let's hope so... And what if the laptop's broken?
B
الشركة بتصلحه. خففي على نفسج، مب أول مرة تصير
ish-sharika bitṣallḥah. khaffifi ʿala nafsich, mub awwal marra tṣīr
The company will fix it. Go easy on yourself; it's not the first time it's happened.
A
صدقت والله. يعطيك العافية
ṣidagt wallāh. yaʿṭīk il-ʿāfya
You're so right. Thanks for your help.
B
الله يعافيج. يلا، خلنا نروح
allāh yʿāfīch. yalla, khallna nrūḥ
Not at all. Come on, let's go.
items: it's no big deal, it's nothing (UAE)
it's all manageable, nothing's that bad
go easy on yourself, don't be so hard on yourself (to a woman)

title: Checkpoint 5.1: Sēf's farewell
